newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says 6 years in power is enough.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says 6 years in power is enough.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Tuesday six years in power was enough for him and dismissed opposition allegations he would engineer a palace coup to install himself as a dictator.

Ramos pledged again his respect for the constitution in an apparent effort to defuse a mounting controversy over moves by senior aides for amendments that would allow him to stay in office for at least six more years after June 1998.

"I say this again to you in your presence, fellow veterans, six years for President Fidel Ramos is enough," the former army general told a convention in Manila of war veterans from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
"We are seeing now the end of coups all over the world. If there are some, they are a declining number," Ramos said.

"There is no way now for any authoritarian regime or a strong dictator, regardless of who he or she may be, can successfully hold the line for any length of time. Here in the Philippines, that will not prosper, I assure you."

His executive secretary, Ruben Torres, sparked the uproar when he said last weekend many members of the administration's Lakas (People Power) party favoured changing the constitution to allow Ramos to stay on after 1998.

The constitution, framed after late president Ferdinand Marcos was ousted after 20 years in office by a popular revolt in 1986, limits a president to only one term of six years. The limit is intended as a safeguard against authoritarian rule.

The political uproar has prompted former president Corazon Aquino, who helped lead the revolt that ousted Marcos, to declare on Monday that she was ready, if necessary, to lead a protest march to thwart any move to change the constitution.
Defence Secretary Renato de Villa, who helped quash six failed army coup attempts against Aquino, said fears of a military intervention were baseless.
"Insofar as military coups are concerned... I think that is history, (it) will not be repeated any more in our time... I would like to allay any fear that there will be any such scenario," he said.
